cards.explanation: The answer is that Ephraim does not even notice. Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice (Hosea 7:9). It's like a cookie box slowly emptying while nobody ever looks inside. The sad part, friends, is that it's his own strength going.

The answer is False. The gray is really there, but the text says “Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.” (Hosea 7:9) So Ephraim is aging and has no clue. Gray hair is one thing, friends, but missing it entirely is something else.

The answer is False. They do not return. Hosea 7:10 says “despite all this, they do not seek Him.” After all of that, they still don't go to Him. Even a loud witness doesn't turn their feet around, friends.

The answer is Egypt then Assyria. The verse says the dove is “…calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.” (Hosea 7:11) Those are two big nations, and Ephraim runs between them. A dove that can't pick a rooftop will wear out its wings, friends.

The answer is His net. The LORD says, “As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the air.” (Hosea 7:12) It fits the bird picture from the verse before. Birds in a net don't get to pick a direction anymore, friends.

The answers are redeem and lies. The LORD says, “Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.” (Hosea 7:13) He would redeem them. That one word shows what He was ready to do, and it makes the lies hit harder, because they speak lies against the very One who would redeem them. That's a heavy line, friends, and it's worth slowing down on.

The answer is False. Hosea 7:14 says they do not cry out to the LORD from their hearts when they wail upon their beds. The LORD says it plainly: “They do not cry out to Me from their hearts…” So the statement is False, friends.

The answer is grain and new wine. The verse says, “They slash themselves for grain and new wine, but turn away from Me.” (Hosea 7:14) This is a heavy part, friends. They go to painful lengths for grain and new wine, and the verse says they turn away from the LORD.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Although I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against Me.” (Hosea 7:15) The verse gives both facts, friends. He trained and strengthened their arms, and they plot evil against Him.

The answer is a faulty bow. Hosea 7:16 says, “They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow.” A faulty bow can't be trusted to hit what you aim at, friends. They turn, but not toward the Most High.

The answer is cursing. The verse says, “Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue…” (Hosea 7:16) That's the reason the verse gives for the leaders falling by the sword, friends. Cursing is the word that fills the blank.
